hook: If you keep getting blindsided by people who "seemed so different at first"
topic: Why people reveal their patterns early — and what we miss
body:
**If you keep getting blindsided by people who seemed so different at first — the signals were there. You just weren't watching for the right things.**

Most people, when they first meet someone, are paying attention to whether they like them. Whether the conversation flows. Whether this person seems kind, interesting, attractive. And that's understandable. But none of those things tell you who someone actually is.

What tells you who someone actually is in those early conversations — is what they do with difficulty. How they talk about people who aren't in the room. Whether the warmth they show you feels personalised, or whether it would work on anyone currently sitting in your chair. How they handle a small moment of friction.

People are not mysteries. They're patterns. And those patterns show up early — consistently, reliably early — but only if you know what you're looking for.

The problem isn't that you're a bad reader of people. It's that you were never taught what to actually observe.

So here's where to start: in the next conversation you have with someone new, don't just notice whether you like them. Notice how they talk about people who have hurt them. That single thing will tell you more than an hour of pleasant conversation.
